text: In the DishBrain system (Kagan et al., 2022), roughly 800,000 cultured human neurons on a multi-electrode array were shown to:
choices: Spontaneously self-assemble into a complete miniature brain with distinct anatomical regions
Modify their activity patterns in response to feedback so as to improve their performance at a simplified game of Pong
Outperform state-of-the-art convolutional networks at large-scale image classification
Continue computing indefinitely with no electronic interface of any kind
explanation: DishBrain neurons received electrical stimuli encoding ball and paddle positions and, after feedback, reorganized their firing to play Pong better than chance, improving across sessions. The authors framed this via free-energy minimization (reducing unpredictable stimulation). It is not a full regionalized brain, not an image classifier, and it depends critically on its electrode interface.
